text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 4.8% today after oil prices spiked on news that Chinese refiners have halted October fuel exports to protect domestic supplies—a move that tightens global fuel availability and supports prices. US crude rose to $96/barrel while Brent jumped above $100, and refineries are running at 92.5% capacity, so higher crude prices directly boost refining margins (the profit refiners make by turning crude into fuel). This follows a week of volatility for the stock, but today's move is clearly tied to the oil price jump linked to China's export suspension.

Geopolitical tensions around Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, plus uncertainty over potential US diesel export restrictions, are adding to the case for elevated energy prices going forward. These supply concerns are supporting the broader backdrop that benefits refiners when crude and fuel prices are elevated.
